text:
maria: heads-up — we got a support escalation. Customer X noticed a sharp p95 jump after last night's runtime rollout (v2.13.4). p95 went from ~120ms to ~420ms for text-gen routes, p99 spikes to ~2s. opening thread.
ben: saw alerts. traces show tail latency concentrated on hotpath kernels. Affected canary hosts = 10%. canary label: runtime=2.13.4-canary
chris: any auth or rate-limit errors? support says no 5xx, just slow responses and some timed-out client requests.
kevin: looking at per-route telemetry now. Quick query: `select p95 from latency where model='redwood-13b' and env='canary'` — yup, spike at 00:42 UTC coinciding with rollout.
lucy: deploy-bot reported successful rollout to canary pool at 00:40: `deploy-bot: rollout finished 2.13.4 -> 10%` :rocket:
ben: I'm seeing increased batch formation time in the canary logs. batch window median up from 2ms to 12ms. suspect kernel selector or batching heuristic change in 2.13.4.
maria: can we repro on a dev host by forcing similar traffic? take one canary instance out of LB and replay sampled requests.
chris: started replay on canary-3. Repro: p95 ~ 430ms locally when using `--weighting=latency-optimized` flag off. If I flip kernel selector to previous strategy, p95 drops to ~115ms.
kevin: that's interesting — change-log for 2.13.4 mentions "kernel-selector: heuristics v2" and "aggressive batching for throughput". Likely the heuristic increases wait time for micro-batches.
lucy: ops-bot shows recent config: `kernel_selector_mode: adaptive_v2` set in canary cluster config.
ben: quick mitigation: temp patch to set `kernel_selector_mode: legacy` for canary rollout. Will apply via runtime-config and watch.
deploy-bot: patch applied to canary pool: `kernel_selector_mode=legacy` by lucy at 00:58 UTC.
kevin: after patch p95 dropped back to ~130ms on canary-3. p99 tail improved as well. Good sign.
maria: ok but we need root cause and proper fix. Could be a bug in adaptive_v2 when seq lengths are short — it overestimates batching benefit and increases delay.
chris: I'll open a bisect candidate list. Suspect commits: kernel-selector heuristic change (commit c3f4), batching-window tune (commit b12a), and kernel-compat fallback (commit f9d1). We'll disable c3f4 locally to confirm.
kevin: while chris bisects, let's hold rollout (pause global rollout) and rollback to canary baseline (2.13.3) for safety? Support asked for immediate mitigation.
lucy: Paused rollout via release manager UI. Not rolling forward. We shouldn't do full rollback yet since config patch already restored behavior for canary.
maria: communicate to support: temporary mitigations in place, monitoring closely. Ask customer X if latency has normalized for them — pinged.
chris: bisect result: disabling commit c3f4 (heuristics v2) removes the extra batch wait — confirmed. c3f4 reproduces latency increase when kernels select micro-batching threshold wrong.
ben: proposed actions: 1) revert c3f4 from release branch 2) harden kernel selector tests with short sequence distributions 3) add telemetry counter for batch-hold-time and an alert threshold
kevin: I'll create quick hotfix branch and bump canary to 2.13.4-hotfix with selector reverted. Then run canary gating with increased sampling.
lucy: support update: customer X confirmed latency back to normal after config change. They'll keep us posted.
maria: thanks team. follow-ups: chris to PR revert + unit tests, ben to add telemetry metric + dashboard, kevin to coordinate hotfix canary + staged rollout, lucy to update postmortem once root cause validated. tagging #oncall for monitoring.
deploy-bot: hotfix branch created at 01:30 UTC. canary rollout scheduled when approved.
ops-bot: alerting baseline restored, will escalate if p95 > 200ms for 5 minutes.
maria: closing thread when hotfix confirmed in canary. great job. :thumbsup:
